design_orientation.scientific_hypothesis: A two-layer stack comprising one SiO2 and one TiO2 layer, with thicknesses bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm, can achieve an arithmetic mean reflectance below 0.03 across the 450-700 nm band at normal incidence if the optimizer finds a non-quarter-wave thickness combination that balances the spectral ripple, or if the optimal solution lies near the quarter-wave points (~98 nm for SiO2, ~60 nm for TiO2) adjusted for broadband performance.
design_orientation.proposed_topology: Air | Layer_1 | Layer_2 | Glass (where Layer_1 and Layer_2 are assigned SiO2 and TiO2 in the optimal permutation found by the optimizer, or explicitly tested as two separate candidates if the solver requires fixed ordering. Here we request the solver to optimize the assignment and thicknesses).

comparability_note: Cross-route target-score ordering is INDICATIVE ONLY. Each route normalizes its soft score against its own executable objective contract; the normalized values are not directly comparable between routes (red line 6). This ranking is used solely to pick the primary recommendation INSIDE the Pareto frontier -- it never removes any solution from the frontier, and every frontier member remains part of the delivered portfolio.

planning_source_comparison.comparison_basis: Cross-arm performance uses frozen-standard representative scores only. Route-local target-score deltas are within-route diagnostics and are not cross-route rankings.
